title: net1 with one value per LCF (expliCCit's encoder), trained on net1 v6's data
description: Does the kind of output explain the gap between our net1 and expliCCit's? net1 v6 states a distribution per LCF (64 bins, three members, the log score). This trains expliCCit's encoder as it is, one value per LCF by squared error, on exactly net1 v6's rows (exp-data-net1-broad-30s-218, -60s-74 and exp-data-net1-v6-221, every 24th step, split by link, the same held-out controllers), in two arms and seeds 0 to 2. Arm ours: net1 v6's settings (robust scaling, dropout 0.05, at most 12 epochs, patience 3). Arm expliccit: expliCCit's settings (min-max scaling, dropout 0.3, at most 50 epochs, patience 5). Each run scores, on the same rows, net1 v6 (seed 0, model-v6-inputs) by the mean of its belief and expliCCit's released net1 (third_party/expliccit-models), which was trained on expliCCit's own data and whose ground-truth definitions may differ from ours. The arm is chosen on the validation rows by mean R^2 over the LCFs; its seed 0 is the net1 that net2 is then trained on. Only these two settings were tried, since net1 v4's grid found settings to matter little (exp-net1v4-grid-10).
run: P=(--set 'output={"kind":"point"}'); if [[ "$ARM" == expliccit ]]; then P+=(--set 'scaling="minmax"' --set dropout=0.3 --set epochs=50 --set patience=5); else P+=(--set dropout=0.05); fi; uv run python experiments/net1_train.py "$OUT/net1-point-$ARM-s$SEED" --spec experiments/specs/net1v4.json "${P[@]}" --seed $SEED --stride 24 --data "$IN/d30/campaign-train30" "$IN/d60/campaign-train60" "$IN/w/campaign-wide30" "$IN/w/campaign-wide120" --ood competitors="$IN/ood/campaign-ood-competitors" --ood loss="$IN/ood/campaign-ood-loss" --ood rtt="$IN/ood/campaign-ood-rtt" --ood buffer="$IN/ood/campaign-ood-buffer" --ood rtt-wide="$IN/w/campaign-ood-rtt-wide" --ood buffer-wide="$IN/w/campaign-ood-buffer-wide" --compare "$IN/m/net1-v6-s0.pt" --compare-expliccit third_party/expliccit-models
